evidence:
Method: built a criterion -> public-requirement map for all 54 criteria (2 gate, 42 functional, 5 polish, 5 visual) in the frozen task, plus every protocol step in tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:33-59 and the polish/visual prompts, against instruction.md, environment/instructions/hireops_rules.md, integration.md and seed_data.json. Read workbook 'Quality Checks' row 28 (#27) and 'Internal Quality Checks' row 28 col E (Mukesh: login is house convention, not graded as unrequired), SKILL.md 'Known false positives' (sign-in, checks 23/27), references/quality-checks.md ### 27, REVIEW_POLICY.md 'No hidden requirements', the template's tests/* prompt shape, and handoffs/LESSONS_FROM_COLDERWATER_2026-10-08.md lessons 1, 7, 12 and 16 (hidden or golden-only demands fail rows 6/27/31).

Every graded demand traces to public text. I found no golden-only rule, exact label, exact route or layout demand:
- Gates: wrong password leaves the visitor signed out, Rafael signs in (instruction.md:19, rules:53); gate_shared add + reload + Observer readback (rules:61,74-75; the Observer reads the board).
- hro_job_open: blank title, places 0/51/2.5 and a recruiter as manager are refused <- rules:70-72 ('whole number from 1 to 50', 'picked from the hiring-manager accounts').
- hro_add_candidate / hro_add_email_rules <- rules:74-79 (bottom of Applied, case-insensitive duplicate per job, message at the field, typed values kept, same address on another job OK).
- hro_move_one_stage, hro_reject_reason, hro_reject_hired, hro_reopen <- rules:90-95 and 128 ('see it move straight away'); rejected-from stage visible to staff <- rules:92 'We like to know where a card was'; reopening clears the reason and undo restores it <- rules:92-93,141-142.
- hro_arrive_bottom, hro_reorder <- rules:99-102. Interview rows <- rules:106-108,143-144. hro_refused_put_back (reason, plus focus on that card's controls) <- rules:128-130 and instruction.md:3.
- Manager, observer, candidate and anonymous rows, and hro_refusal_status statuses 401/403/404/409 <- rules:64-66,110-116,121-122,243-244. The candidate 403-or-404 alternative is accepted, which matches both rules:65 and rules:66.
- hro_stale_refused 'says ... by whom' <- rules:120-124 and instruction.md:3. The ABA case (F returns to Applied) is fair because rules:120 says the version changes on every move.
- Bulk rows (board order, all-or-none, places counted for the whole set) <- rules:134-137. Undo rows (place restored; blocked by anyone's move, re-order or reject; a note or another card doesn't block; once only; a later move supersedes; overfill refused) <- rules:141-146.
- hro_activity (who, what changed, rejection reason, newest first, per-job filter, Observer reads, no line for refusals) <- rules:156-160 and 61.
- hro_notes <- rules:150-151. hro_live_board and the polish live rows (15 s, no reload, keep the open card, typed text, focus, scroll and open conversation) <- instruction.md:5 and rules:164-170.
- Message rows: plain text/<b>, non-blank, line breaks kept, Enter/Shift+Enter, box empty and focused after send <- rules:186-188. Latest 30, oldest first, scrolled to newest, 30 at a time, remaining count, place kept <- rules:192-195 and seed thread_page_size=30.
- Unread/seen rows <- rules:199-214. The seeded Lena count of 1 checks out against the seed (APP-301 has 3 messages, USR-CAN3 read_count is 2, and the 3rd message is from USR-REC3). Bill as the job's manager marks the candidate message seen <- rules:213.
- hro_thread_access <- rules:178-182. Drafts (per conversation; survive switching, reload and session end; sign-in prompt; not visible to others on the same browser) <- rules:218-223 and instruction.md:7. Note-draft persistence <- rules:152 'keep it for me on that browser until I do'.
- Candidate rows: wording table <- rules:232-239 and seed candidate_status_labels. The seed matches Noor's PE (Infrastructure/INTERVIEW), Noor's PD (Design/APPLIED) and Tomas's DA (Finance Systems/SCREEN). The privacy list (notes, reason, rejected-from stage, board place, other candidates, activity, including SSE/socket payloads) <- rules:241-244 'nothing their browser receives'. hro_candidate_linked <- rules:78-79.
- hro_restart: the seeded order (Greta, Ade, Marco / Priya, Samuel) and Noor's note match the seed positions and notes[0]. Durability <- instruction.md:17 and integration.md:27-28.
- Visual Likert rows grade generic desktop craft. The visual prompt (line 14) leaves layout and labels to the implementer and requires no phone layout or theme switching (instruction.md:11).
- Flexibility where the brief is silent: dragging is optional; hiding refused actions is optional (functional prompt:31); any route or label (app_context.md:37-38); a wrong-password message is optional; Activity may combine a multi-card move into one line; notes need not appear in Activity; candidate board/Activity reads may return only the candidate's own data; the stale refusal may identify the person by an id.

Conforming alternatives considered: (a) an app that hides the Interview control when it is full is accepted by hro_refused_put_back's third route if the card shows why; (b) an app returning 404 for a candidate's move on someone else's card is accepted; (c) per-column or page scrolling are both allowed by the polish row; (d) an app that does not log notes in Activity is accepted. Broken app that could pass: none found through an unrequired-detail loophole. That direction is coverage, which other rows own.

Residual notes (not demonstrated defects, kept as risk):
N1 (P3) Undoing a rejection (hro_reject_reason) and a reopening (hro_reopen) depends on reading reject/reopen as a 'move'. rules:141-142 supports that reading: 'gives back a rejection reason the move removed' is only possible if a reopening is an undoable move. rules:88-95 also put reject/reopen under 'Moving a card'. But rules:143 and rules:156 list moves, rejections and reopenings separately, so a builder could plausibly limit undo to stage moves. The owner may want one requester-voice clause, e.g. that rejecting or reopening counts as a move for undo. Row 6 owns ambiguity.
N2 (P3) hro_pol_live_board requires 'the scroll offset is what it was before the move'. Suppose the judge scrolls the page to the very bottom and the other recruiter moves a card out of the tallest column. The browser then clamps scrollY even though the app left scroll alone. The golden board scrolls the window (styles.css:65-68 gives the columns no max-height). This could false-fail a correct app. Fix: say 'scroll it to the middle', or have the other recruiter move a card in a different, shorter stage. Feasibility is mainly row 32.
N3 (P3) hro_refused_put_back says 'no reason is shown on or for that card'. The judge might fail a global toast such as 'Interview is full' that does not name the card, though the brief only says 'tell me why'. Similarly, hro_seen 'shows as not seen' could be read as needing an explicit not-seen label rather than the absence of 'Seen'; the brief's 'shows whether it's been seen' supports either. Both are wording-level risks only.
N4 (P3) hro_anonymous requires 401 for every replayed read, so a server-rendered app that 302-redirects page reads to sign-in would fail. rules:64 states '401' explicitly, so this is a stated requirement, not an unrequired one.
Sign-in itself is a known false positive (SKILL.md Known false positives; Internal sheet note). In any case the brief lists the accounts and has candidates sign in.

Evidence limits: this is source mapping only. The raw golden harness output (qc/repairs/hireops-2026-10-03-workspace/results/workspace.json, sha256 7df855f4dd1f2d9ecda15f7eb4578d1f1b653e6158c49ebda4244ba3862a9760, matches raw-evidence-index) is scripted, not a configured judge run. No Oracle, model or judge-behaviour measurement exists, so the judge interpretations in N2/N3 are unmeasured.
suggested_fix: Optional hardening, not blocking: add a requester-voice clause that rejecting/reopening count as moves for undo (N1); in hro_pol_live_board, scroll to the middle or have the other recruiter move a card from a shorter stage (N2); let hro_refused_put_back accept a refusal message shown right after the attempt that concerns that move (N3).
